housing.summary: Jyvaskyla is a university city in Central Finland with a comparatively affordable rental market versus Helsinki. Most rentals are handled through national listing portals and private landlords; student housing (KOAS) is significant given the large student population. Furnished units are less common. Leases usually require a security deposit and proof of income.

banking.summary: Opening a Finnish bank account typically requires a Finnish personal identity code, a valid passport/ID, proof of address, and often proof of employment or residence permit. Strong authentication (online banking credentials) is central to Finnish daily life for services and logins. Major banks operate branches in Jyvaskyla.

schools.summary: Public education follows the Finnish national core curriculum and is free, including comprehensive school (peruskoulu). English-language and international schooling options are limited compared with Helsinki, but some IB-track and English-medium provision exists at upper-secondary level. Early childhood education (varhaiskasvatus) is municipally organised.

legal_admin.summary: New residents must register with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV) to obtain a Finnish personal identity code and register their municipality of residence. EU/EEA citizens register their right of residence; non-EU nationals need a residence permit from Migri before registration. Municipal services in Jyvaskyla are then accessed via the registered home municipality.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register at DVV for a personal identity code and municipality of residence; non-EU nationals must first obtain a residence permit from Migri

tax_finance.summary: Workers must obtain a tax card (verokortti) from the Finnish Tax Administration (Vero) so the correct withholding rate is applied to salary. The tax card requires a personal identity code. Non-residents staying under six months may be taxed at source. Vero provides guidance and an online service (OmaVero) for tax matters.
tax_finance.tax_id_name: Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus) / tax card (verokortti)

transport.summary: Local public transport in Jyvaskyla is operated as the Linkki bus network, covering the city and surrounding municipalities. Travel cards and mobile tickets are available with season/monthly options. The city is bike-friendly. EU/EEA driving licences are valid; non-EU licences may need to be exchanged within a set period. Healthcare is arranged through the wellbeing services county (Central Finland) with social insurance via Kela.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences valid as-is; non-EU/EEA licences generally must be exchanged within a limited period after establishing residence, subject to bilateral recognition rules
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with the Central Finland wellbeing services county for public healthcare; apply to Kela for social insurance coverage
